Hi Priyom,

Thanks for sending over the MSA and order form. Procurement and Legal at Acme had a couple of fairly targeted asks on the Term and Renewal language before we can move to procurement approval:

- Auto-renew: Acme requests a 90-day opt-out window prior to renewal rather than 30 days.
- Termination for convenience: we need mutual termination for convenience with a 60-day notice period and pro-rated refund for pre-paid fees.
- Survivability: Acme wants certain obligations (data return & deletion, audit rights) to survive termination for 12 months.

Can Redwood accommodate these without changes to pricing? If not, please flag which items require CRO/Finance approval. I've attached our internal preferred redline to this thread.

Team / Sarah — I reviewed Acme's redline. Notes below by clause: 

1) Auto-renew / Notice: Acme requests 90 days. Risk: longer notice reduces our ability to re-price or reallocate capacity quickly. Suggest compromise: 60-day notice for annual renewals, 90-day for multi-year by exception. Alternatively, include a SCC (Service Commitment Clause) that preserves price guarantees for the term and offers a one-time 90-day opt-out for the first renewal only.

2) Termination for convenience: Mutual 60 days is acceptable if we limit refunds to unused prepaid fees on a pro-rata basis (and exclude any committed reserved capacity charges that were already consumed). Add language to cap aggregate refund to remaining unearned prepaid balance.

3) Survivability: 12 months for data return/deletion is reasonable. Keep narrow definitions for what 'audit rights' mean (scope, frequency). We should avoid open-ended audit remedies.

If Sales is willing to accept the 60-day/60-day compromise and pro-rata refunds capped to prepaid balance, I can prepare a clean redline for Acme to review. Otherwise, we'll need approval from Finance to accept uncapped liabilities.

-LB
Laura Bennett
Counsel, Contracts & Commercial
Redwood Inference

Tom / Sarah — appreciate the clarity. Summary of Redwood position and proposal: 

- Auto-renew notice: Redwood can accept a 60-day opt-out for annual renewals (compromise from 30d standard; we typically don't offer 90d). For multi-year deals we can consider 90d on a case-by-case basis.
- Termination for convenience: Mutual termination with 60-day notice is acceptable. Refunds will be pro-rated and apply to unearned prepaid subscription fees. Refunds will exclude consumed reserved capacity and any non-refundable implementation/third-party costs. We will add an explicit definition of 'consumed reserved capacity'.
- Survivability: Redwood accepts 12-month survival for data return/deletion and limited audit rights (scope and frequency to be defined).

Next steps: Laura will prepare a clean redline reflecting the 60-day compromise + pro-rata refund cap to remaining unearned balance. If Acme signs that, we can route for e-signature. Aditya — finance confirmation on pricing exposure?
